Durable local log anchors and atomic two-slot pin switches. Logical compaction and verified recovery; physical WAL cleaning and general backup retention remain pending.

Exclusive two-slot I/O; data and file-name sync precede root publication.

Bounded ordered deadlines with exact scoped tokens, replacement/cancellation and lateness. TimedShard supplies automatic consensus timer management through this public seam.

contracts.scope: Bounded one-use admission-to-effect-lease map, exact runtime/worker/visit checks, pre-admission output reservation, original rejection ownership, duplicate/stale rejection, fenced provider failures and drain continuations. Native three-node/100-group TCP/TLS snapshot catch-up and actual-file recovery with native runtime providers; explicit elections and automatic heartbeats, plus a separate timer-driven election/partition/healing history. Three-node/100-group integration covers replication, read barriers, retries, leader replacement and actual-file restart.
Injected nonblocking completion hint, never durable evidence. Shared host resources remain host-owned.

PeerTransport consumes dispatched batches and returns them for exact completion after buffer release. Local completion is not a Raft acknowledgement or persistent delivery claim.

Independent wire format 1 for all current static-configuration RPCs, same-peer multiplexing, fixed validated prefix, bounded lengths/counts/decoded retention and trusted peer-scope consistency. Native worker and recursive snapshot histories traverse frames. A host-only single-fixture provider tests the public seam, not full alternative codec conformance. No socket/authentication or wire snapshot chunk protocol.

TLS 1.3 mutual authentication, trusted peer certificate pins and authenticated recovered store-session hello. Bounded nonblocking I/O progress and handshake byte/time ceilings; host-supplied resources and generations. PeerTransport uses this same public seam. Real loopback TLS/wire/worker histories plus partial-I/O, backpressure and failure tests. Simulator-only providers rejected.

Authenticated connection-level multiplexed frames, bounded prefix-first receive allocation, one pending/terminal send and one decoded receive, separate channel/plaintext poll budgets and original outbound-batch ownership until buffer release. Explicit security capability and boxed provider forwarding. Partial I/O, backpressure, failure and close tests. Real three-node/100-group TCP/TLS plus actual-WAL worker/restart history now traverses PeerRoster, including quiescent reconnection. Complete listener/dial and ingress/result assembly remain pending.

contracts.scope: Construction-authorized identities, bounded connection/handshake reservations, host-reserved checked generation ranges, fair polling, monotonic reconnect deadlines/backoff, stale attempt/input rejection and exact accepted-send lifetime through retirement. No membership or quorum authority.

Explicit bounded TCP dial worker, checked node/store/session/generation tickets, nonblocking connected streams, exact cancellation and terminal credit lifetime, failure/drain/join. Native TCP/TLS histories dial through this public contract. Channels are unauthenticated address results; production listener/routing/TLS handshake ownership and full node admission remain unfinished. Timeout bounds one connect call, excluding queue delay; roster deadlines require cancellation.
Explicitly seeded reproducible election jitter; independent node seeds supplied by host. No cryptographic/identity use.
